PA-2025-HB2886.title: An Act amending the act of June 27, 2006 (1st Sp.Sess., P.L.1873, No.1), known as the Taxpayer Relief Act, in taxation by school districts, further providing for public referendum requirements for increasing certain taxes.
PA-2025-HB2886.aiSummary: The bill would change the Taxpayer Relief Act rules for school district taxes. It would update when a public vote is needed before certain school taxes can go up.

PA-2025-SB1415.title: An Act amending Title 18 (Crimes and Offenses) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, in assault, further providing for the offense of neglect of care-dependent person and for the offense of abuse of care-dependent person; and, in sexual offenses, further providing for the offense of institutional sexual assault.

votes.motion: FINAL PASSAGE
Committee vote (Judiciary): Reported as Committed

PA-2025-SB1415.aiSummary: The bill would raise some penalties for harming or neglecting care-dependent people, including making certain neglect and abuse crimes felonies instead of misdemeanors. It would also make institutional sexual assault by a caretaker against a care-dependent person a more serious felony. The act would take effect 60 days after passage.

PA-2025-SR412.title: A Resolution directing the Legislative Budget and Finance Committee to conduct a performance audit of pharmacy benefit arrangements under the Commonwealth's Medical Assistance managed care program, including the use of public resources, payment transparency, applicable requirements, Department of Human Services oversight and beneficiary pharmacy access and report its findings and recommendations.
PA-2025-SR412.aiSummary: The Senate resolution would direct the Legislative Budget and Finance Committee to audit pharmacy benefit arrangements in Pennsylvania’s Medical Assistance managed care program. It would look at public spending, payment details, state oversight, and how well people can get pharmacy care. The committee would then report its findings and recommendations to the Senate.

PA-2025-SR409.title: A Resolution urging the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission to evaluate and approve the addition of the American Paddlefish to the Species by Watershed Approved for Open System Propagation and Introductions list.
PA-2025-SR409.aiSummary: The resolution urges the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission to review and approve adding the American Paddlefish to a state list that allows regulated fish breeding and stocking. It would affect the commission and those who work on fish propagation and stocking in Pennsylvania waters. The text says the goal is to support conservation and fisheries management.

PA-2025-HB2790.title: An Act amending Title 12 (Commerce and Trade) of the Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes, providing for video streaming services.

actions.text: Referred to Consumer Protection & Professional Licensure

votes.motion: Committee vote (Appropriations): Re-report Bill As Committed
FINAL PASSAGE
Committee vote (Communications & Technology): Report Bill As Committed

PA-2025-HB2790.aiSummary: The bill would add rules for video streaming services in Pennsylvania. It would bar ads from having louder audio than the video they play with, and it lets people file complaints with the Attorney General’s consumer protection office. If a service breaks the rule, the Attorney General could seek a civil penalty of up to $5,000 for each violation and other court relief. The act would take effect in one year.

PA-2025-HB2545.title: An Act providing for insurance coverage for vaginal estrogen for the treatment of menopausal symptoms and urinary tract infections.

actions.text: Reported with request to re-refer to Aging & Older Adult Services
Re-referred to Aging & Older Adult Services

votes.motion: Committee vote (Appropriations): Re-report Bill As Committed
FINAL PASSAGE
Committee vote (Aging & Older Adult Services): Adopt Amendment A04309
Committee vote (Aging & Older Adult Services): Report Bill As Amended
Committee vote (Insurance): Re-refer Bill To Another Committee

PA-2025-HB2545.aiSummary: The bill would require health insurance plans in Pennsylvania to cover vaginal estrogen for treating menopausal symptoms and for preventing urinary tract infections. It would apply to plans issued or renewed after the law takes effect, and it would cover FDA-approved drugs, devices, and combination products used to provide vaginal estrogen. The coverage could still be subject to plan rules like medical need checks, cost sharing, and review. The act would take effect 90 days after passage.

PA-2025-HB1827.title: An Act providing for medical assistance coverage and insurance coverage of screening, prevention and treatment measures for osteoporosis as a result of menopause.

actions.text: Reported with request to re-refer to Aging & Older Adult Services
Re-referred to Aging & Older Adult Services

votes.motion: FINAL PASSAGE
Committee vote (Appropriations): Re-report Bill As Committed
Committee vote (Aging & Older Adult Services): Adopt Amendment A04355
Committee vote (Aging & Older Adult Services): Report Bill As Amended
Committee vote (Insurance): Re-refer Bill To Another Committee

PA-2025-HB1827.aiSummary: The bill would require medical assistance and health insurance plans in Pennsylvania to cover screening, prevention, and treatment for osteoporosis for people who have reached menopause. It includes bone density testing, certain medicines and devices, and some prevention steps like dietary supplements, physical therapy, and weight training or personal training services. The new rules would apply to some plans when filed or renewed on or after the set dates in the bill, and the act would take effect in 90 days.

PA-2025-SR401.title: A Resolution designating the week of October 19 through 23, 2026, as "School Bus Safety Week" in Pennsylvania.
PA-2025-SR401.aiSummary: This resolution would designate the week of October 19 through 23, 2026, as "School Bus Safety Week" in Pennsylvania. It would also urge motorists, parents, and students to follow traffic rules around school buses and help keep children safe. The resolution would also thank Pennsylvania school bus drivers for getting students to and from school and related activities safely and on time.

PA-2025-HB1346.title: An Act amending the act of May 17, 1921 (P.L.682, No.284), known as The Insurance Company Law of 1921, in casualty insurance, providing for menopause treatment coverage.

actions.text: Reported with request to re-refer to Aging & Older Adult Services

Committee vote (Appropriations): Re-report Bill As Committed
Committee vote (Aging & Older Adult Services): Adopt Amendment A04311
Committee vote (Aging & Older Adult Services): Report Bill As Amended
Committee vote (Insurance): Re-refer Bill To Another Committee

PA-2025-HB1346.aiSummary: The bill would require health insurance plans in Pennsylvania to cover hormone and non-hormone treatment for menopause symptoms. It would include FDA-approved drugs and devices, behavioral therapy, and treatment for menopause caused by a hysterectomy. The coverage would follow the plan’s normal rules on medical need, cost-sharing, and review, and it would apply at different times depending on when a plan is filed, issued, or renewed.

PA-2025-HB2336.aiSummary: This law adds work zone safety to driver training and testing in Pennsylvania. Teens under 18 who want a junior driver's license must show they printed or viewed state materials on distracted driving and unsafe driving in work zones. The driver's manual and the written test must also cover how to drive safely in a work zone, and the law takes effect 60 days after approval.
